eliyah-rabbah/1:_: [1] Even if mixed, etc.—that was placed in it when it was still fermenting, for mustard prevents it from fermenting further and preserves it in its sweetness; and Maharil permitted leaving it but not drinking it on Passover. And see siman 453 seif 4 regarding nullification in majority; Chok Yaakov answered that here it is not called a mixture since it is made for its taste. One can also say that there it fell by itself and here it is mixed by hand. It also appears to me that there he takes it back out, which is not so here—it remains in it.
eshel-avraham/1:_: And must not leave it—see siman 462. And regarding whether one is specifically obligated to burn it, see siman 445.
kaf-hachayyim/1:_: (1) [Seif 1] Mustard or other types of condiments—with which one dips meat, and they contain vinegar and other things that have acidity, and people are accustomed to put flour in them, for flour also becomes chametzed through acidity. R' Zalman wrote (1) and this is from Rashi Pesachim 40b.
